pages.title: Mini Game Introduction
pages.text: ■ Fading Affection is a choice-based text adventure mini game that allows you to view the records of people caught up in the Silver Gun Project.

pages.title: Starting the Mini Game
pages.text:
■ Press the Initiate Recording button to start the game.
■ You can play as many times as you want.

pages.title: Routes
pages.text:
■ Fading Affection has three different routes for you to explore.
■ Each route will be unlocked according to a schedule.

pages.title: Unlocking Routes
pages.text:
■ Some routes are locked by default.
■ Locked routes will be unlocked at their designated times.

pages.title: Choices
pages.text:
■ The choices you make in Fading Affection determine the direction of the story.
■ The events that take place will change according to your choices.

pages.title: Locked Choices
pages.text:
■ Some choices can only be unlocked after meeting certain conditions.
■ You can view the conditions needed to unlock a choice via the choice itself.
■ Simply select the choice to get a hint about how to unlock it.

pages.title: Returning to Previous Choices
pages.text:
■ If you make a wrong choice, you can press Return to go back to a previous scene.
■ When you return to a previous scene, your previous progress made from choices after that scene is erased.

pages.title: Status Info
pages.text:
■ In Fading Affection, the main character in each record has a status that indicates their current condition.
■ A character's status may play a role in opening up certain directions in the story.

pages.title: HP
pages.text:
■ This indicates a character's health.
■ HP will increase or decrease depending on the choices you make.
■ When a character's HP reaches 0, they die.

pages.title: Food
pages.text:
■ This indicates the rations in a character's possession.
■ Food may be required to select certain choices.

pages.title: Corruption
pages.text:
■ This indicates the degree to which a character is corrupted.
■ Corruption will increase or decrease depending on the choices you make.
■ If a character's corruption gets too high, they will become fully corrupted.

pages.title: Saving Memories
pages.text:
■ Memorable moments experienced by a character will be saved to their NIMPH in the form of memories.
■ Saved memories are the key to unlocking new choices.

pages.title: Viewing Memories
pages.text:
■ All saved memories will be recorded in the Memories menu.
■ You can press the Memories icon while playing to view the character's saved memories.

pages.title: Endings
pages.text:
■ Your choices will inevitably lead you to an ending in the story.
■ There are multiple types of endings - "Death End," "True End," etc.
■ Try to get all the endings by making different choices.

pages.title: Ending Recollections
pages.text: ■ You can view the endings you have already seen in the Recollections menu.

items.name: Saved Memory: Rapture Attack
items.description: I can't let my guard down on the surface. There's no telling how or when a Raptures might attack. I'll have to be more cautious next time.

items.name: Saved Memory: Trap
items.description: There was a crossbow trap inside the convenience store storeroom, and beneath it, I think I saw a cat and the silhouette of whoever set it up... Next time I go inside, I'll have to be mindful of the trap.

items.name: Saved Memory: Patrol Time
items.description: I was in such a hurry that I didn't realize there were aerial-type Raptures patrolling as well. No matter how much of a rush I'm in, trying to push forward while Raptures are patrolling seems like a bad idea. Next time, I should head out at a different time.

items.name: Saved Memory: Pack Behavior
items.description: Ground-type Raptures aren't the only ones patrolling. There were some aerial types that came by afterwards. Next time, I'll need to find a way to take on both types of Raptures.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Large Road
items.description: There's nowhere to take cover in the middle of that large road. Choosing to fight head-on was reckless. Next time, I shouldn't fight them there without a plan.

items.name: Saved Memory: Stamina Management
items.description: Continuing to sprint just because there was nowhere to take cover was never going to end well. And here I thought Nikkes had infinite stamina... I'm not sure there's anything I can do about the mental exhaustion, though. Next time, I'll have to keep an eye on my stamina while I'm on the move.

items.name: Saved Memory: Range of Fire
items.description: What was I thinking? I can't believe I tried to snipe a target with no consideration for my gun's range... I must've really been in a hurry. It's honestly a little embarrassing. Next time, I'll at least check how far my gun can shoot before opening fire.

items.name: Saved Memory: Collapsing Ceiling
items.description: I rushed. I was in far too much a hurry. Why was I so scared and anxious? I don't remember... Regardless, I shouldn't just dash into some random building next time. Shelter always needs to be chosen carefully, no matter what kind of hurry you're in. It's where you have to spend the night, after all.

items.name: Saved Memory: Gunshot
items.description: In the end... I couldn't bring myself to choose my own demise. It's not a decision that can be made lightly. Death is... a truly terrifying thing.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Hunter
items.description:
I read what the hunter wrote in the storeroom of the convenience store. Why did someone with such a strong will to live choose to die by overdosing on sleeping pills?
Because they were alone?
... Will I also become like that someday?

items.name: Saved Memory: The Cat
items.description:
I saw a cat in the storeroom of the convenience store. When I offered it some of my rations, it gobbled it right up. It must've been really hungry.
Once it finished eating, it was like life had returned to its eyes. It was really beautiful. It rubbed affectionately against my legs as if to thank me, almost like it was sharing its warmth. I really liked it.
Life can be so radiant and warm.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Black Smith
items.description:
The Black Smith was roaming the residential neighborhood. It whipped around its tentacles almost silently in the darkness and dragged me away before I could even react.
It's dangerous. Far too dangerous...
I need to be careful in the old downtown district after dark.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Warmth of Life
items.description:
I was so scared and anxious. Life felt completely meaningless. But just when I was about to give up, that cat showed me the warmth that life still had to offer. It was as if the cat were telling me that my life had meaning, too.
The life I had saved ended up saving me in return.
It turns out there's still meaning in this unending loop of a life. So... I'm not going to give up. I'm going to keep moving forward, just a little further.

items.name: Saved Memory: Trail
items.description:
The little side road behind the residential neighborhood leads to a trail that reaches the lake, which means there's a way to get to the lake without taking that large road after all.
How did the cat know about that trail? If I ever see it again, I'd like to thank it properly... I wonder if I'll ever get the chance.

items.name: Saved Memory: The End of the Large Road
items.description: There was a huge hole at the end of the road, blocking the way to the lake. There's no point in taking this path anymore.

items.name: Saved Memory: Raptures by the Lake
items.description:
There was a Black Smith near the lake, too. Had it always been there? Or did the one from the old downtown district follow me?
Whatever the case, it's dangerous.
I never thought I'd have to see one again once I got out of the old downtown district. How am I supposed to evade it and run away with the lake there?
... How many times will I have to die and come back this time?

items.name: Deleted Memory: The Repository
items.description:
This must be a memory of her being devoured by the Black Smith.
She was broken down and melted... It's horrific...
...
I'm going to erase this.
The fear and the trauma will be too much for her.

items.name: Deleted Memory: Fall
items.description:
She chose to take her own life on the surface...
Why doesn't her fear disappear?
What am I doing wrong?
...
I'll erase this. I'll erase it, and we'll start again.

items.name: Deleted Memory: Freedom
items.description:
This is a memory of her... envying a bird in flight.
She wanted to be free. At the time, she must've felt like a bird in a cage...
...
I should erase this. Those sorts of feelings will only interfere with her mission. Once she starts yearning for freedom, she'll only keep wanting to escape from this place.
Heh. That's so... cruel.
I'm just another cruel cage for her.

items.name: Deleted Memory: Betrayal
items.description:
She said she'd betrayed me, calling her brief desire to stray a betrayal. Just the tiniest show of self-interest, and she calls it a betrayal.
What a kind, poor soul...
...
I know that, and yet I'm still erasing this memory... I'm the one betraying you, not the other way around.
... I'm sorry.
I'm so sorry, Maria.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Importance of Memories
items.description: I'm sure my memories from my time as Maria, back before I was called Marian, have meaning too. They're what brought me this far, after all.

items.name: Saved Memory: Hypervigilance
items.description:
I overreacted because I thought I had to protect the Commander. I opened fire without even checking whether it was a deer or a Rapture. And because of that, the Commander died shielding me.
... This can never happen again.
I'll make sure to confirm my target before pulling the trigger next time.

items.name: Saved Memory: The Commander's Stamina
items.description:
It may sound obvious, but the Commander is human, which makes him different from a Nikke. He needs food and rest, or else he's bound to run out of stamina.
I failed to consider that.
Next time, I need to be more considerate of his needs.

items.name: Saved Memory: Sacrifice
items.description:
The Commander shielded me from the Black Smith... He threw himself in front of me so I wouldn't die. As if I deserve that. As if I won't just come back anyway, no matter how many times I die.
Why would he do that...?
I can't keep letting him sacrifice himself like that. I can't keep letting him die in agony.

items.name: Saved Memory: Electrocution
items.description:
I was so focused on running from the Black Smith that I didn't even notice the building was flooded, or that the water was electrified. But even if we managed to hide, it's not like we could stay in there forever. Hiding isn't how I protect the Commander in the long term.
I'll try to fight back next time, no matter how scary it may be. If that's what it takes to protect him, I think I can do it.

items.name: Saved Memory: Priorities
items.description: Being melted inside Black Smith was horribly painful. And yet, the weird thing is... I was satisfied just knowing that I'd saved the Commander. Death used to terrify me, but now I think I'm more afraid of seeing him die.

items.name: Saved Memory: Shattered Window
items.description:
Today I learned that the windows on that building can't support a Nikke's weight. I still can't believe I fell through one right in front of the Commander... For some reason, I'm kind of embarrassed.
To look at it another way, though, now we know we can break those windows. I wonder if we could use that against the Black Smith somehow.

items.name: Saved Memory: Timing
items.description:
I was being too cautious because I was afraid of falling through one of the windows. But this is a Black Smith we're up against; if I keep underestimating it like that, we'll never be able to defeat it.
I have to focus and give this fight everything I've got in order to protect the Commander.

items.name: Saved Memory: A Nagging Feeling
items.description:
Something feels strangely familiar about this place, and about what the Commander said and did. If something meaningful happened here, I should be able to remember... I'd have those memories.
What am I forgetting? What is this nagging feeling?
I can't recall any of it right now, but I have to get myself to remember. I have to. I can't shake this feeling that it's important.

items.name: Saved Memory: Building a Dream Together
items.description:
There's nothing I can do right now about this terrible corruption, or this mission. All we can do is the best with what we have.
So I'm going to complete this mission however I can, and choose to believe that things will turn out all right, just like how the Commander extended his hand to me when we were struggling with our false purpose.
And I'm going to dream of a future, one where I can live by his side once all this is over. As long as I have that dream, as long as there's still hope that it might come true... I can keep going, even through this hell.

items.name: Saved Memory: Company
items.description:
That was kind of surreal. I would've died for sure if I had been alone, but I was able to escape certain death simply because there was someone else here. Just having someone by my side opened up a new possibility that hadn't been there before. 
... It's weird to think about.

items.name: Saved Memory: A Happy Life
items.description:
He said that we could be happy, that all this suffering would end someday and we could finally be happy. I know there's no way that's possible... That truth has been pounded into me again and again as I've died more times than I can count.
And yet... oddly enough, I still want to believe him.

items.name: Saved Memory: A Look of Fear
items.description:
The Commander looked at me and was scared. It was only for a split second, but I'm sure there was fear in his eyes. Why, though? I've never done anything that would make him afraid of me...
... At least, I don't think I have. Maybe there's something wrong with my memory. What if I've been doing something bad without even realizing it? He wouldn't look at me like that for no reason. That's not who he is.
He's kind.

items.name: Saved Memory: Walking Together
items.description:
I'm sure he was afraid of me, so then why did he reach his hand out again? As if it was the most natural thing in the world, just like the first time we held hands. After everything that's happened, after all the frightening things he's been through, he still reached out without hesitation.
His hand is so warm whenever I hold it. It makes me feel like everything I've been so anxious about will turn out all right, almost like the warmth from his hand enters into my heart...
As long as the Commander is by my side, I feel like everything will be okay.

items.name: Saved Memory: Shared Scenery
items.description:
The lake was as beautiful as ever. That beauty used to make my life feel even more hopeless by contrast, but with the Commander by my side, I could finally enjoy it. It no longer felt so sad, lonely, or hopeless.
All I could think about was how much I wanted to see this shimmering scenery with him again.

items.name: Saved Memory: Concerned Eyes
items.description:
What did he mean by "still okay"? Was the Commander waiting for something to happen? Did he mean something would change at some point?
He was looking at me when he said it... Does that mean there's something about me that changes?
There's so much that I don't understand, but I can't bring myself to ask... His eyes were so full of warmth and concern when he looked at me. I'm afraid that warmth will disappear...

items.name: Saved Memory: Shared Meal
items.description:
The Commander didn't have to share his food with me. I'm a Nikke. And yet he still offered me some, saying that food tastes better when you share it with someone else.
I know he was only saying that so he could give me half, but it really did taste better than when I'd eaten alone. The ingredients and everything were the same as before, but somehow, just eating it together with him made it taste better.
It's so odd how that works.
Now that I've experienced it... will I ever be able to eat alone again, without the Commander by my side?

items.name: Saved Memory: End of the Forest
items.description: There was a huge crevice at the end of the forest north of the lake, blocking the way forward. There's no point in trying to take this path to get to the industrial complex anymore.

items.name: Saved Memory: Frantic Behavior
items.description:
The Commander wasn't acting like himself. He was in a hurry, like he was being chased. It almost seemed like he was trying to protect me from something...
I vaguely remember being struck by Black Smith's tentacle the last time, when we were searching for another building to hide in.
Did something happen to me then?
Why can't I remember what happened next? What happened to the Commander after that?

items.name: Saved Memory: A Future Together
items.description:
The Commander wants to protect me, and I want to protect him. In this terrifying place, we're both just relieved to have each other.
I can't believe we feel the same way...!
... It makes me so happy.
I want to find ways to become even happier with him by my side, with this person who shines with such warmth... I want us to have a happy future together.

items.name: Saved Memory: Cooperation
items.description:
The Commander asked to go down the building with me, saying he was afraid to wait alone, but I knew he was lying. He came with me because he was worried about me, worried that I'd feel lonely or scared.
How is he so kind and caring?
I never knew fighting by his side could make me this happy. I feel a warmth spreading through my heart.

items.name: Saved Memory: Revenge
items.description:
We finally defeated the Black Smith, the monster that claimed the lives of countless Marias, Marians, and Commanders.
Our victory could never make up for all those lives lost, but I think we were at least able to exact a small measure of revenge. And the fact that we defeated it together makes me happier than words can express.

items.name: Saved Memory: A Life that Shines
items.description:
You told me you'd only made it this far because you had me by you side. Whenever I hear your kind words and meet your warm gaze, even my once-worthless life seems to shine brilliantly.
You makes me feel like I'm worthy of love. You turn me into the most precious person in the world.
How could I not fall in love with someone like you?

items.name: Saved Memory: The Truth
items.description:
I've been... killing the Commander. I become corrupted and then kill him.
How could he look at me with such tender eyes? Did he really mean it when he said he wanted a future with me? I want to ask him, but I'm not sure if I have the right to...
I'm sorry, Commander. I'm so, so sorry.

1101.text:
Maria heads toward the old downtown district, which is closer to her transport ship.
Trees and wild foliage have grown in between the cracks of collapsed buildings and shattered roads. The desolate remnants of war left behind by the Raptures welcome Maria.

1102.text: Suddenly, the ground begins to rumble. Maria hears a series of loud, ominous thuds coming from beyond the building ruins.

condition.hint: Since the sounds still seem far away, ignore them and press on.

1103.text: Whatever's making the noise still seems to be some distance away. Figuring she'll be fine as long as she moves quickly, Maria sprints toward a nearby building...

1104.text:
One must never let their guard down on the surface.
Maria quickly ducks behind some nearby debris for cover. A ground-type Rapture leaps over the building and lands nearby with a crash. Thankfully, there's only one.
"It's alone... I can handle it," Maria tells herself.
Sticking behind cover, Maria successfully launches a counterattack. She takes down the Rapture and presses onward.

1105.text:
Maria arrives at the large plaza of the old downtown district. With the surrounding structures reduced to rubble, only three routes remain open to her.
She chooses to...

options.text: Go left, toward the commercial district.
Go straight, toward a residential neighborhood.
Go right, toward the large road.

1106.text: Maria decides to check the commercial district to her left first, hoping to find something useful.

1107.text: Maria decides to search the residential neighborhood ahead of her for a path to the lake.

1108.text: Maria decides to head toward the main road on the right to see which route she needs to take.

1109.text: Among the collapsed buildings, Maria finds a run-down convenience store that's still intact. She peers through the shattered glass door and spots a can of food lying on the floor. However, the interior is too dark for her to make out much beyond it.

1110.text: The door creaks open as Maria steps into the convenience store. She figures it's best to salvage as much food as she can, no matter what it takes.

1111.text:
Maria decides to explore the commercial district a little further.
However, no matter how much she looks around, she finds nothing of interest. She decides to return to the plaza.

1112.text:
Maria picks up the can of food she spotted from outside.
"It's empty..."
She glances around the store, disappointed, and notices an open storeroom. She gazes into the pitch-black room. Something metallic glints in the darkness.
"I wonder if there are more of these inside..."

1113.text:
Maria steps into the storeroom.
As soon as she does, a metallic clank rings out.
"!!!"
She feels a sharp pain shoot through her ankle. Looking down, she sees a semicircular metal trap bolted to the floor, now clamped around her ankle.
"Why is there something like this in here...?"
Suddenly, something clicks beneath her foot.
Almost like a switch.
A sinking feeling washes over Maria...

1114.text:
It's too dark inside the storeroom.
Wary of what dangers might be lurking inside, Maria gives up on scavenging for canned food and leaves the convenience store.

1115.text:
"If I remember correctly, there's a trap just ahead..."
Maria peers deeper into the storeroom. Sure enough, there's a trap on the floor.
Suddenly, she hears a meow.
"... Was that a cat?"
A strange sense of déjà vu envelops Maria as she recalls the memory of getting caught in the trap and dying. There had been a cat beside the hunter in the darkness.
"You're the cat I saw back then..."
The cat stares intently at her, as if it, too, recognizes her.
There may still be someone inside the storeroom, or they may be gone; Maria can't tell from where she is.

1116.text:
Maria jumps over the trap near the entrance of the storeroom and follows the cat inside. Beneath the crossbow trap in the far corner of the storeroom, she sees a crouched figure...
"Oh..."
... The hunter's skeleton.
Several articles lie scattered across the floor: empty food cans, seemingly eaten by the hunter when he was still alive, an open pill case, a powered-off flashlight, and an empty water bottle.
Maria picks up the pill case.
"... Sleeping pills."
She then looks down at the red writing scrawled across the floor.

"I'm scared. I'll stay hidden in here and kill anyone who tries to come in. I have food, and I set up a trap. If I just stay here and hold out, I'll survive.
"I just need to hold out a little longer. I have to survive, no matter what. I'm scared.
"I'm scared. I don't want to die. I want to live."

Maria's gaze lingers on the final sentence:
"But why exactly do I want to live?"
Maria quietly sets the pill case back down.

1118.text:
Maria searches the storeroom a little longer, but quickly realizes that there's nothing left to find.
The cat meows at her expectantly, as though it wants something from her.

options.text: Share some rations with the cat.

condition.hint: Save your rations.

1119.text:
The packaging rustles as Maria pulls out a piece of dried jerky and gives it to the cat. The cat enthusiastically chomps down on it and rips off a piece that it chews on for a while. Judging by how frantically it's gnawing at it, it must've been starving.
As it finishes, the cat meows and looks up, its eyes sparkling with renewed vigor.
"!!!"
Maria finds herself unable to look away from the beautiful light of the cat's eyes. She feels as if she is seeing the light that is inherent in life. As Maria continues to stare, the cat walks up to her and rubs its head against her leg.
"Hehe, how cute..."
After gazing at Maria for a moment, the cat jumps over the trap and runs out of the storeroom. Maria watches it go before stepping over the trap herself and following it out.

1120.text: She can't spare food here when she doesn't know when she might need it later. Though it may seem cruel, Maria tells herself that this is the right decision. She turns away from the cat and walks out of the storeroom.

1121.text:
Maria leaves the storeroom and begins to make her way out of the convenience store.
Just then, the heavy footsteps of approaching Raptures echo from outside.

options.text: Hide behind the shelves and wait it out.

condition.hint: Waiting would take too long. Try going outside.

1122.text: There's no time to waste. She must use every second to get even a little closer to her destination. With this in mind, Maria steps out of the convenience store.

1123.text:
It's best to lay low when Raptures are on the move. Maria hides herself behind the convenience store shelves so that even aerial-type Raptures won't be able to spot her.
She hears Raptures whizzing by in the air and thudding along on the ground.
After what seems like forever, Maria no longer hears any movement outside. She peers out the window. There are no Raptures in sight, either on the ground or in the air.
"Now I can leave."
She steps outside.

1124.text: Maria feels the ground rumbling as she enters the residential neighborhood. She spots a pack of Raptures patrolling the area. Taking them down would be the safest way to ensure she can take a proper look around.

options.text: Avoid them and go back to the plaza.

1125.text:
A single pack of Raptures seems manageable. She should fight them, if only to see how much stronger she's become.
Maria readjusts her grip on her gun and charges forward.

1126.text:
Drawing on her past experiences, Maria watches the pack of Raptures for a little longer.
The thumping of their footsteps continues as five Servant-class and five Master-class ground types pass by first, followed shortly after by three Servant-class and two Master-class aerial types.
"Just as I suspected... There were both ground and aerial types."

1127.text: This doesn't seem like the right time to engage. Maria quickly abandons the idea and decides to return to the plaza.

1128.text: Maria contemplates whether to engage or to go back.

options.text: Fight while making use of the environment.

1129.text:
Maria decides that confronting them head-on would be too dangerous and comes up with a different strategy.
She observes the Raptures' path and the surrounding terrain. Then, she notices a rusted crane near where the aerial-type Raptures are circling. There's only one cable supporting the crane.
"At this distance... I could hit that cable."
She waits for the aerial-type Raptures to draw closer to the crane.

1130.text:
The massive crane comes crashing down, knocking the aerial-type Raptures down to the ground.
"Now!"
The Raptures' formation is disrupted and, seizing the opening, Maria calmly dispatches them one by one, starting with the aerial-type Raptures. Before long, she kills the last of the Raptures that were patrolling the neighborhood.

1131.text:
"I didn't realize it had already gotten this late," Maria murmurs, gazing up at the sky awash with the colors of sunset. She can feel the night fast approaching.
She wonders whether to continue exploring for a little longer or start looking for a place to set up camp for the night.

options.text: Find a place to set up camp immediately.

1132.text:
The sun hasn't completely set yet. Maria decides to make use of the remaining light and press on for a little longer.
However, before long, the sun disappears completely, and darkness cloaks the city. It's hard to see almost anything. Maria realizes she made the wrong choice.
"I need to find a place to set up camp immediately..."
Just then, something slices through the air with a sharp whoosh.
"!!!"
A tentacle suddenly reaches out from the darkness and snatches her up.

1133.text:
Chills run down Maria's spine.
She begins to feel strangely anxious.
She knows she must run.
She must find somewhere safe.
She must avoid [[REDACT]]the repository[[/REDACT]]dangerous places.
She decides to...

options.text: Get inside quickly, no matter where.
Calm her nerves and take her time searching.

condition.hint: Something seems to be coming. Quickly get inside somewhere.

1134.text:
An inexplicable fear consumes Maria's mind. She hurriedly searches for somewhere to spend the night. Anywhere will do, so long as there are no Raptures.
After frantically scanning her surroundings, she finds a building with no sign of any Raptures.

1135.text:
Choosing where to spend the night is an important decision. Maria decides to take extra care, despite being in a hurry, and slowly searches for somewhere to stay.
Soon, she finds a relatively intact building with a small window.
"This place looks safe enough."
Maria sets up a decoy before cautiously stepping into the building.

1136.text:
After setting up a decoy, Maria steps inside and slumps to the ground. With the sun fully set, she can't see a thing outside.
"I guess... I'll rest for a bit."
Maria leans her head against the wall and closes her eyes.
However, not long after, her eyes shoot open as an inexplicable sense of anxiety grips her. She took every precaution before entering the building, and yet an inexplicable fear fills her mind.
She wants to pour out all her worries to someone, but...
"... There's no one here."
She is alone in the dark.
Loneliness suffocates her.

1137.text:
Maria nervously clutches her gun. It feels as though the Raptures could barge in any moment if she were to put it down.
"It's okay... It's all okay. Everything will be all right," she tells herself.
But her anxiety doesn't stop. She can't even bring herself to close her eyes.
"Why do I feel so anxious?"
The fact that she doesn't even know where this anxiety comes from only makes it worse.
"Am I... broken?"
Then, a thought strikes her.
"My life has no meaning anyway... Shouldn't I just die and then ask the doctor to fix me?"
Maria gazes down at the gun clenched tightly in her hands.
She brings the muzzle to her chin.
"Now... pull. Just pull... the trigger..."
Maria places her trembling finger on the trigger.
"Ngh... Ahhh...!"

condition.hint: Try entering the storeroom inside the convenience store.
Try sharing rations at the convenience store.

1138.text:
With a loud bang, the bullet blows a hole in the wall. Maria realizes that she turned her head away from the muzzle.
"Ah... Ahhh...!"
She loathes herself for being so afraid of even death that she can't make a decision.

1139.text:
Maria thinks back to the final words the hunter had written in the convenience store storeroom:
"But why exactly do I want to live?"
"Why do I want to live?" she wonders. "What meaning is there in a life like this?"
No amount of thinking seems to yield an answer for her.

1140.text:
Suddenly, Maria hears a meow.
"!!!"
Startled by the sudden noise, she turns around. The cat she saw at the convenience store is staring up at her.
"It's you again..."
The cat walks up to her and butts its head against her leg. Maria feels warmth from this little life in front of her.
"Oh..."
The gun clacks as she sets it down. Instead, she picks up the cat and cradles it in her arms. The cat lets out a soft meow as it nestles contentedly against Maria.
Maria feels the warmth of its body—the warmth of a life she saved.
"There is meaning after all... This life has meaning."
Holding the cat close, Maria closes her eyes. She is no longer anxious or afraid.

1141.text:
A meow awakens Maria from her slumber.
"!!!"
She opens her eyes. Sunlight spills in through the window.
"It's morning...?"
Only then does she realize that she had fallen into a deep sleep. She gently pets the cat's head as it sits beside her.
"Thank you. I got a good night's rest with you here."
The cat gets to its feet and leisurely trots out of the building. Maria watches it for a while before picking up her gun.
"Time to get going again."

1142.text:
When Maria steps outside, the cat readily greets her with a meow.
"You haven't left yet, huh?"
The cat meows at her once more and begins to walk away. Then, it turns around and meows at her again.
"Do you want me to... follow you?"
The cat meows as if to affirm. Maria follows after the cat.
After a short while...
"There's a path here..."
Maria finds herself in front of a path with a sign that reads, "Lakeside trail." Surprised, she looks down at the cat, only to find that it's no longer there.
"Where did it go...?"
She looks all around, but the cat is nowhere to be seen.
"..."
She decides to follow the trail.

1143.text:
Maria finds a large road that leads to the lake. If she passes through the lake area, she'll be able to quickly reach the target location. However, there doesn't seem to be anywhere she could take cover in case of a Rapture attack.
She considers whether to risk it and press on, or turn back and take a safer route.

options.text: Wait for Raptures to show up and snipe them from a distance.

condition.hint: Try to run as far as possible first.

1144.text:
"Might as well give it a shot."
Maria decides to take her chances, since death isn't a huge issue for her anyway. Just making the attempt will provide valuable experience.
Having made up her mind, she runs down the large road.

1145.text: Maria knows from previous experience that going down a large, open road without a plan is reckless. She decides to find cover near the entrance of the path and wait for Raptures so she can snipe them before proceeding.

1147.text:
After running along the road for some time, Maria hears the whirring of a pack of aerial-type Raptures closing in overhead.
"They got here faster than I expected..."
She wonders whether to keep running or engage them in combat.

condition.hint: It seems dangerous to just keep running. Fight off the Raptures first.

1148.text:
Maria stops in her tracks and turns around to engage the aerial-type Raptures that are closing in.
There's only one problem.
She still doesn't see anywhere to take cover on the deserted road.

1149.text:
She shouldn't engage; there's no way she'd win. She decides to sprint as fast as she can this time, all the way to the end of the road.
The sound of the Raptures closing in sends a chill down her spine as she's reminded that she died here last time.
She keeps her eyes on the path ahead of her.

1150.text:
Maria hides behind a row of recycling trash cans outside a nearby maintenance building. Just as in previous experiences, she senses a pack of aerial-type Raptures approaching, as though they're on patrol.
"I'm nervous..."
She finds herself gripped by an anxiety she can't identify; whether due to her previous death or something else, she can't tell.

options.text: Shoot at the Raptures as soon as they come into view.
Hold back the anxiety and use bait.

1151.text: Maria grows increasingly antsy from her inexplicable anxiety. She pulls the trigger as soon as an aerial-type Rapture comes into view. A loud bang echoes across the road.

1152.text:
"Stay calm..."
Maria regains her composure and calmly takes a glass bottle from one of the trash cans and throws it ahead of her.
The bottle hits the ground and shatters.

1153.text:
She fires rapidly at the aerial-type Raptures as they dive toward the shattered bottle, taking them down one by one. After a long battle, she finally manages to kill all of the aerial-type Raptures.
"I finally got them!"
Basking in an inexplicable sense of exhilaration, she looks around cautiously.

1154.text:
Maria continues down the road for a long while, heading toward its end. Thankfully, no Raptures ambush her along the way.
However...
"The road's been cut off."
A huge hole has opened up in the road, and she can't go any farther. She's disappointed that she can't take this road to the lake, but she also feels a sense of accomplishment at finally seeing the end of the road she'd been curious about.
"Time to head back."
Maria makes her way back to the plaza.

1201.text: Using all the saved memories she has accumulated, Maria determines the best route to the lake.

1202.text: She follows the lengthy road and walks for quite a while, until finally she spots a vast lake glistening in the sunlight.

options.text: There's no time to admire the scenery. Press onward.
Take in the view of the lake.

condition.hint: There's no time to look at the lake. Keep moving forward.

options.text: Run in the opposite direction from the target location.

1203.text:
Maria presses onward, encouraged by the thought that she's one step closer to the target location. There's a pack of Raptures near the lake, but drawing on the combat experience she has gained so far, she is able to make her way forward without any trouble.
Suddenly, the ground rumbles.
Thump, thump, thump.
Maria looks up ahead.
"!!!"
A Black Smith is drawing close.
"So there's a Black Smith here, too..."
She tightly grabs her gun.

1204.text:
Maria thinks about the Raptures by the lake. She starts to dread the idea of having to die, come back, and kill Raptures all over again.
"I think... I need some rest."
She stares blankly at the glistening lake in the hopes of feeling better. In stark contrast to her situation, the lake shines brilliantly.
Just then, she hears the faint trill of a bird drifting through the air.

1205.text: Suddenly, the thought strikes Maria that she can't just keep doing this. She needs to escape this endless cycle of death and become free. She shoots one last glance at the glistening lake, and then dashes in the opposite direction of the target location.

1206.text:
Maria hurriedly looks around.
She sees a small bird flapping its wings on a tree not far from her. Upon closer examination, she sees that its leg is caught on a nylon cord wrapped around a branch.
"I know I should save it, but..."
The branch stretches out over the lake. One wrong move, and she could easily fall in.

1207.text:
Maria runs toward the tree to save the bird. She leans as far over as she can and starts untangling the cord from the branch.
The bird chirps.
"Okay, all done!"
As soon as Maria frees the cord, the bird wildly flaps its wings.
"Ack...!"
Maria's body lurches back, tipping her completely toward the lake.

1208.text:
Maria concludes that there shouldn't be any more variables standing in the way of her carrying out her mission. She tears her gaze away from the lake and starts heading forward.
Suddenly, she feels the ground rumbling.
Thump, thump, thump. 
In an instant, she finds herself face-to-face with the Black Smith.
"I won't get killed this time...!"
She tightens her grip on her gun...

1209.text:
Maria looks down.
One of the Black Smith's tentacles is piercing her body.
"Urk...!"
She hurriedly rips out the tentacle and, steeling herself, begins to fight back.
"I have to defeat it...!"
Time passes as she fights...

1210.text:
She wonders if this really is the right choice. Should she just turn back now?
"Maria."
Even though she knows the doctor no longer watches her in real time, Maria keeps feeling as though she hears her voice.

condition.hint: Try investigating the residential area at night.

1211.text:
She comes to a halt.
She finds herself panting, and even starts to cough. She knows a Nikke's body shouldn't be gasping for breath after running this short a distance, but for some reason she feels almost like she's suffocating.
"Maria-n!" Doctor Maria's voice echoes clearly in her ears.
"Doctor...?" Maria calls out blankly.
"Where are you right now? Why are you over there...?!"
"I didn't realize... you were watching me today."
"Huh?" Doctor Maria sounds taken aback. "Well... You've been acting strange lately."
Maria is glad she stopped. She's glad she didn't choose to betray her.

1212.text:
She feels as though the horror she had forgotten would resurface if she were to stop here and return to her mission. Yet, alongside that feeling, another memory stirs within her.
"Once again, it's nice to meet you, Maria-2."
"... Hm? Your name?"
"Oh... Well, I made you based on myself, so that's just how I named you."
The more she remembers, the slower her steps become.
"Maria..."
She still feels like she can hear Doctor Maria's voice in her ears.
She hesitates.

condition.hint: Try pulling the trigger on the night when anxiety had left you utterly exhausted.

1213.text:
Maria starts to think.
She can't remember it all clearly, but she recalls the countless deaths she must have experienced, and the emptiness of the endless new beginnings that followed each one.
She is filled with sadness at her pitiful future, where she will leave the transport ship and walk toward death again, and again, and again. Hers is a life that leaves nothing behind, a life in which she can speak to no one, a life without meaning. A life that exists solely for death.
She is sick and tired of it all.
However, alongside that feeling, another memory stirs within her.
"Why not start from 1? I guess because 1 is... me, haha."
Maria remembers the doctor's laugh that she let out to hide her embarrassment that day. She remembers her warmth. Her voice.
"You and I now share the same fate."
Her shared fate. Her creator. Her mother.
Another her.
"Maria."
Her own voice rings in her ears.
She catches her breath as she sees the edge of the mission area.
This is it. This is where it ends. With just one more step, she will be outside of the map—outside of the mission area.

condition.hint: Try saving the entangled bird.

1214.text:
This is a betrayal, and Maria knows it. Even so...
"Ngh... I'm sorry. I'm so sorry...!"
Clutching her sadness, longing, guilt, and remorse close to her heart, she runs beyond the mission area towards the freedom she had yearned for.

2101.text:
Marian gazes at the old downtown district, a place she must've seen hundreds of times. She recalls her deaths that didn't leave behind so much as a trace, and countless moments of loneliness.
But this time, it's different.
"Shall we, then?" the Commander says.
She is not alone.
Marian and the Commander set out on the path in front of them.

2102.text: Upon stepping into the old downtown district, Marian feels the ground rumble in an all too familiar pattern.

2103.text:
She opens fire. Drawing on her memories of taking down dozens and even hundreds of Raptures, she easily dispatches the lone Rapture.
"Enemy down. Please come this way, Commander."
"Marian, watch out!"
"!!"
The Commander fires at another Rapture that is coming down, seemingly having jumped from high up.
"There was another one...?!"
Marian follows suit and fires at the Rapture. Before long, the Rapture lifelessly slumps down.
"I'm sorry. There was only ever just the one here..."
Marian reproaches herself. She can't believe she let her guard down yet again. If she had been alone, she surely would've died without being able to react.
"That's okay. This is the good thing about working as a pair, right?" says the Commander with a laugh.
"A pair..." Marian says to herself.

2104.text:
One must never let their guard down on the surface.
Marian pulls the Commander along and quickly ducks behind some nearby debris for cover. A ground-type Rapture leaps over the building and lands nearby with a crash.
"I knew it...!" she whispers.
Before long, another heavy thud shakes the ground, and a second Rapture appears.
"There are two of them...?!"
A chill runs down her spine as she and the Commander fight side by side, taking down both Raptures.

2105.text:
"That was different from before," she says, and then firmly adds, "I shouldn't let my guard down."
The Commander nods. "I trust you."
As Marian feels the weight of responsibility settle upon her, the two continue forward.

2106.text:
"Want to keep going?" asks the Commander. He takes a step forward.
Something stirs within Marian as she looks at him, and she falls into step beside him.

2107.text: Marian arrives at a familiar plaza with the Commander. She takes a moment to recall how to get to the lake.

condition.hint: Recall Maria's memory of following the cat.

2108.text:
Just as Marian is about to hurry toward the lake, she hears the Commander ask a question.
"Is there anywhere you'd like to stop by before we go?"

options.text: Go to the convenience store to check if the cat is there.
No. It's best to just hurry forward.

condition.hint: You feel uneasy leaving without taking a look. Stop by the convenience store.

2109.text:
"Commander, this is bad...!" Marian cries out in a panic. "I don't remember how to get to the lake!"
"... What?" the Commander replies, somewhat dumbfounded.

2110.text:
"I'd like to go see... a cat..."
"A cat?"
"There's this cat that showed me the way to the lake. I'd like to check on it if I can..." Marian hesitates. "But we should probably hurry over to the lake, right?"
Noticing her hesitation, the Commander says, "There's no rush. If you want to go check on it, we should."
"... Thank you."
"Lead the way."
Marian leads the Commander to the commercial district, and before long, the convenience store from her memories comes into view.
"This is it."

2111.text:
"No, I don't think so. There's nothing else I need to do."
Suddenly feeling an inexplicable anxiety, Marian decides it would be best to head to the lake as soon as possible.
"Oh... Okay. Sure."
The two of them leave the old downtown district behind and keep moving.

2112.text:
The door creaks as Marian pushes it open and steps into the dark interior of the convenience store. As always, she's greeted by nothing more than a few empty food cans.
"I don't think it's here..."
Marian looks at the storeroom. It seems as dark as ever.
"Shouldn't we check in there as well?" the Commander asks.
"Oh... I suppose so. It's just..."
She recalls the hunter inside the storeroom.

2113.text:
"There's a trap right in front of the entrance, so I'll go in by myself."
"Marian?"
Marian steps over the trap and enters the storeroom alone.
"Looks like it's not in here, either..."
The only thing left inside the storeroom is the hunter's skeleton, lying there all alone, the same as before. Marian looks down at the words written on the floor: "But why exactly do I want to live?"
"..."
She now understands their loneliness.
"Did you not want me coming in here because of this skeleton?"
"!!!" Marian flinches. "Commander..."
He stands next to her.
"They must've holed themselves up in here..." The Commander gazes at the writing on the floor. "That's really unfortunate."
Unable to stop herself, Marian asks, "Why do you think this person wanted to live, Commander?"
"It's hard to say..."
"Sorry. You don't have to answer...!"
"They probably believed that all this suffering would end someday, and that they would eventually be happy."
"... You think it was because they believed they'd be happy someday?"
"Yeah, and that belief must've made them try their best to survive."
"... Do you think we could be happy someday, too?"
"Of course," he says. "I'm sure of it. That's why we need to keep fighting with everything we've got."
"..."
The Commander extends a hand to Marian. "Wanna get out of here?"
Marian silently takes his hand.

2114.text: Marian and the Commander step out of the storeroom and are about to leave the store when they hear the heavy footsteps of Raptures outside.

options.text: Hide behind the shelves and wait it out.

condition.hint: Stay hidden a little longer to protect the Commander.

2115.text:
Marian recalls her past experience and hides behind the shelves with the Commander.
The pack of Raptures whirs and thuds loudly as it passes by.
More time passes than expected.
Marian stares outside without moving an inch.
"..."
The Commander breaks the silence. "I think we can leave..."
His words are interrupted by another rumble.
"Huh... There are more coming. We'll have to wait a little long—"
"We need to go."
"Marian?"
The Commander turns to face her.
"!!!"
Her eyes are red.

2116.text:
A sense of foreboding washes over Marian. They shouldn't wait it out. They need to go...!
She stands up.
"Marian...?"
"We need to go."
"!!!"
The Commander's face freezes in fear.
"Commander...?"
He relaxes his expression. "S-sorry about that! So... why do you think we should go?"
"Something tells me we shouldn't stay here for long," Marian replies. "I just... have a feeling."
"..."
The Commander slowly examines Marian's face.
"Okay. If that's the reason, let's go," he says. "I'm sure we'll be able to take them down together."
"... Right."
Marian slowly examines the Commander's face in turn.
"... Marian?"
"It's nothing. Let's go."
Marian heads outside, still thinking of the expression on the Commander's face.

2117.text:
"We need to go."
Marian rises to her feet and starts walking outside.
"We need to go. We need to go. We need to go. We need to..."
"Marian!!"
The [[REDACT]]Commander[[/REDACT]]—no, [[REDACT]]No. 7[[/REDACT]]—no, the [[REDACT]]Commander[[/REDACT]]—no, [[REDACT]]No. 7[[/REDACT]]the man calls out to Marian, but she doesn't look back.

2118.text: "Marian!" The man grabs her and calls her name.

options.text: Shoot [[REDACT]]no one! Do NOT shoot [[/REDACT]]the man.

2119.text:
Marian shakes off the man and points her gun at him. The gun clicks.
Horror spreads across his face.

2120.text:
The last burst of gunfire echoes in the air.
"All clear."
Marian and the Commander successfully defeat the pack of Raptures without suffering much damage.
"Good thing we decided to leave," the Commander remarks.
"... Yeah."
Marian gazes at the convenience store they had been hiding in. A nagging sense of unease creeps over her, as though she's forgetting something.
"Shall we get going, then?" the Commander asks.
"Sure. Now that there's nothing more to take care of, we can head straight to the lake."
They're still a long way away from their destination, so they decide to keep pressing forward.

2121.text:
Marian walks over to the trail leading to the lake with the Commander.
"If we keep following this path, we'll reach the lake. I'll lead the way, just in case..."
"Marian."
"Yes?" Marian turns around.
"Here."
The Commander holds a blue rose out to Marian.
"A rose...?"
"I noticed that they're growing here too."
The Commander points at the side of the road. Only then does Marian notice the blue roses dotting the roadside.
"You're... right. I didn't realize this place had them too."
"You've been tense for the last while now. What's wrong?"
"What...?"
"Nothing bad is going to happen. So why don't we..." The Commander pauses, extending his hand toward her. "Have a nice walk together?"
"!!"
"I read on the sign that this is a walking trail. It'd be a shame to spend the whole walk so tense."

2122.text:
Marian gazes silently at the hand that's being held out to her, before shifting her eyes to his face.
"Are you just gonna leave me hanging?"
There's no sign of fear in his eyes, as if nothing happened earlier. Her unnaturally heightened senses are warning her that she definitely did something wrong, but after looking into his eyes, Marian finds herself wanting to believe that nothing really did happen.
"No, of course not," she says. She wants it to be true so badly.
Marian takes the Commander's hand.
The Commander beams. "Now, ready to go for a walk?"
"... Yeah."
His hand is warm this time too, just like when they first held hands.
"I'm ready." Marian smiles back at him.
Strangely enough, she no longer feels afraid of herself.

2201.text: Using all the saved memories they have accumulated, Marian and the Commander determine the best route to the lake.

2202.text: After walking for a long while, Marian and the Commander spot a vast lake glistening in the sunlight.

options.text: Take in the view of the lake.

2203.text:
"Seeing how we made it all this way, why don't we enjoy the view for a bit?"
"It's dangerous to get too close. You might fall in and..."
"Still, we gotta see it up close, right?"
The Commander pulls Marian closer to the lake.
"Wow, just look at that. It's so pretty." He smiles, gazing at the lake as it shimmers beneath the sun.
"..."
Marian stares at his bright smile, entranced, before turning her head to look at the lake.
"What do you think, Marian? This is nice, right? It really helps clear your mind."
"Huh...? I..."
She recalls all the countless deaths she experienced here by herself.
"... Yeah, it really is pretty."
And yet, just by taking in the view with him here, she doesn't feel as lonely, desolate, or hopeless as before.
"Let's make sure to come back here again," he says.
"... Yeah, definitely."
A thought takes hold of Marian: she wants to protect him, even if only so that she can enjoy this view with him again.

2204.text: Marian and the Commander realize that this isn't the time to leisurely gaze at the lake. They decide to admire the view another time.

2205.text: They don't have the luxury of getting distracted. The two of them head toward the collapsed building along the trail to fight the Black Smith there.

2206.text:
"Want to get going now?"
Marian and the Commander peel their eyes away from the lake and decide to move on.

2207.text: Marian and the Commander look for a path forward at the lake. To reach the target location, they could either pass through the northern forest to the industrial complex, which would be faster but more dangerous, or they could take the southern walking trail, which is relatively well maintained but would be a longer detour.

options.text: Head south along the walking trail.

condition.hint: Speed is of the essence. Head to the northern forest first.

2208.text:
"The fastest way to reach the target location is to pass through the northern forest and head over to the industrial complex. For the sake of our mission, going that way would definitely be the right choice, but..."
Marian's face darkens.
"When I was here before... there was a Black Smith roaming the area." Marian's hand trembles. "I'm worried we might encounter it again."
The Commander takes her hand. "It'll be all right."
Marian looks up and into the Commander's eyes.
"You're not alone this time. Let's give it a try."
"... Sure."
Marian wants to say that being together with him makes her afraid that she won't be able to protect him, but instead she forces a smile.

2209.text:
"It might be a longer detour, but following the walking trail to the south should be safer," Marian mutters to herself. "The chances of us running into the Black Smith would be lower too, meaning the Commander won't need to sacrifice himself again..."
"... Marian? Are you all right?"
"Hm...? Oh, yes. Of course. I'm fine."
"..."
"We should get going."
Marian takes the lead and starts walking ahead. The Commander watches her without a word.

2210.text: Marian and the Commander arrive at the edge of the northern forest. A few trees lie fallen, likely knocked over by Raptures in passing.

options.text: Move toward where there are more trees, albeit with less visibility.
Move toward the clearing, where there's less cover but more visibility.

condition.hint: Having places to take cover would be safer. Head into the denser part of the forest.

options.text: Go back and take the other route.

2211.text: Marian concludes that having more cover would be better in the event of a potential Rapture encounter. She and the Commander head toward the thicker part of the forest.

2212.text: Remembering the hardships that come with limited visibility, Marian and the Commander decide to head into a more open part of the forest with a clearer view.

2213.text: Marian and the Commander decide they have nothing else to investigate in the forest. Instead, they quickly head for the walking trail.

2214.text:
Now that they've reached the denser part of the woods, they don't see any Raptures, but their progress slows to a crawl with their visibility compromised. Marian stays on high alert, her nerves on edge with the fear that the Black Smith could ambush them at any moment.
"Whew..." the Commander exhales.
"Are you tired?"
"No, I'm all right. What about you? Staying on guard must be exhausting."
"I'm okay, too." Marian smiles.
Just then, they hear something rustling nearby.
"!!"

2215.text:
Marian swiftly fires a warning shot... but there's nothing there save for a deer.
"!!!"

2216.text:
Marian and the Commander raise their weapons and aim, only to see...
"... A deer?"
"!!"
Calming herself, Marian lowers her gun.

2217.text:
The deer prances away as soon as Marian lowers her gun.
"I think the limited visibility here has got us on edge." The Commander smiles sheepishly. "Maybe we should relax just a little bit."
"Right."
Marian follows his lead and relaxes her shoulders.

2218.text:
The Commander and Marian continue moving forward for a long while before they stop and take a look ahead. The thick canopy of trees make it difficult to make out how much farther they have left to go.
"Do you think we should turn back before it's too late?" asks the Commander.
Marian suggests that they...

2219.text:
"We've already come all this way. I think we should keep going until we reach the end of the path."
"All the way to the end?"
The Commander looks at Marian worriedly, then responds.
"Yeah, sounds good. We may as well see this through to the end."

2220.text: Marian's instincts warn her that they must not stay in the woods any longer. They decide to backtrack to where the paths diverged.

2221.text:
Marian and the Commander head deeper into the forest. After quite some time, the Commander suddenly realizes that the scenery looks eerily similar to what they saw an hour ago.
"Marian, I think we've been here before. Should we check the map again?"
"..."
"... Marian?"
The Commander looks back at Marian.
"Your eyes...!"
Marian's eyes have turned red.
"Since when...? We haven't even run into any Raptures..."
"..."
Marian's red eyes stare at him blankly.
"Is it because we've taken so long? Was she designed to become corrupted if she takes too long? But why...?"
"I have to go," Marian says, taking a step forward.
The Commander grabs her by the arm. "Go where?"
"I have to go."
"Marian!"

2222.text:
"I have to go. I have to go. I have to go. I have to go." Marian shakes off the [[REDACT]]Commander[[/REDACT]]man and keeps walking.
"Marian!"
"I I I have have have to to to go go go."
Just as he tries to stop Marian again, he feels the ground rumbling.
"No way... Is she calling Raptures to our location?!"

options.text: "I I I have have have to to to go go go."

2223.text:
With fewer trees around, their visibility has greatly improved...
However, they almost immediately hear ominous whirrs coming from above. They spot a swarm of aerial-type Raptures roaming the sky. Marian knows that if the two of them move too quickly, they'll likely be forced to engage.

options.text: Keep an eye on their movement and walk with caution.

condition.hint: Fighting over and over again is dangerous. Move carefully all the way to the end.

2224.text: Marian decides that battling too frequently while accompanying the Commander would be unwise. They advance slowly and cautiously, remaining wary of the Raptures' movements.

2225.text: Now that Marian knows a Black Smith is following them, she decides that they don't have the luxury of taking their time. However, since running might put them at greater risk, they decide to walk as briskly as possible.

2226.text:
Some time passes. Navigating around the Raptures proves more time-consuming than expected.
Marian sighs. "This is taking longer than I thought."
"Yeah..." After a moment of serious reflection, the Commander tentatively gives a suggestion. "Why don't we speed up a little bit?"

options.text: Agree to pick up the pace.

2227.text:
Marian feels as though the Commander seems strangely anxious. A wave of unease settles over her as well.
"All right, then I think we should start running. Will you be okay?"
"I'll be fine. I'll keep up with you."
"Okay."
Marian adjusts her grip on her gun and breaks into a run.

2228.text:
Marian expresses her desire to stick to their current pace, saying that moving cautiously is safer, albeit slower.
"That's true, but..."
The Commander looks into Marian's eyes with concern.
"Hm... Still okay."
"Commander?"
"Oh, sorry... I didn't mean to stare," he says. "All right, let's keep going at this pace." He smiles as though nothing is wrong and then starts walking forward. 
Marian follows behind him with the concern she saw in his eyes still weighing on her.

2229.text:
The aerial-type Raptures relentlessly rain down lasers, causing explosions all around.
The Commander is out of breath, and his stamina only continues to deplete. Marian is also struggling, unable to find a way forward.

2230.text:
Just then, they feel the ground rumble.
Thump, thump, thump.
"You've got to be kidding...!"
Marian and the Commander turn around. Sure enough, they see the Black Smith. It whips its tentacles towards Marian.
"!!!"
A fear that was drilled into her countless times freezes her in her tracks.

2231.text:
The Commander and Marian keep up a swift walking pace. After some time, the Commander's stomach rumbles loudly. The sound startles Marian.
"Sorry...!"
"Oh, you must be so hungry. Maybe we should stop and eat something."
Marian looks around.

options.text: There's no good spot to eat. Eat later.

2232.text:
"Why don't we eat somewhere around here?"
Marian sits under the biggest tree in sight. The Commander sits down beside her.
"Thanks," he says. "I was actually at my limit."
"I'm sorry. I should've been more considerate..."
"Not at all. This is helping me increase my stamina."
"Hehe, is that so?"
She hands him her only piece of jerky.
"Aren't you going to eat?"
"I'm okay. I'm a Nikke. I can get by without eating."
"Don't you have any more jerky, though?"
"No... I still only get one ration, despite there being two of us now. I think it's supposed to be a part of the test."
"Oh... I see."

2233.text:
Marian is anxious that the Black Smith might appear at any moment. Nowhere feels safe.
"I'm sorry, but I don't think it's safe enough for us to eat here."
"That's okay. Let's go a little farther and eat later."
"Thank you, Commander."
The two of them decide to press on for a little while longer. However, no matter how far they walk, there's no place among the trees that they can rest at ease. Their breathing grows more labored and they start to slow down without proper sustenance.
Suddenly, ominous thumps reverberate through the ground.

2234.text:
"..."
The Commander splits the jerky in half.
"Here," he says, offering half to Marian. "Let's share."
Marian gazes at it quietly.
"Go ahead. Take it."

2235.text:
Bewildered, Marian accepts the half-piece of jerky.
"You really didn't need to..."
"Nikke or human, you still have to eat. Besides, food tastes better when you eat with someone else."
"I see..."
The Commander pops his half of the jerky into his mouth. Marian watches him for a moment before doing the same.
"... It tastes good."
From just a dry piece of jerky, Marian feels a wave of warmth spread through her heart.
... At the same time, she grows even more afraid at the thought of losing him.

2236.text:
"Ready to get going?"
The Commander and Marian quickly walk toward the other end of the forest. However...
"What the...?"
The forest floor is split by a giant crevice several meters wide. The two of them peer down, but it's so deep that they can't see the bottom. It almost looks as though there had been a massive earthquake.
"This isn't marked on the map..." the Commander says.
"It must've happened in just the past few years."
"I don't think we'll be able to leap across."
"Agreed..."
Marian looks to the other side. Although it's still far away, the industrial complex where their destination lies is within view.
"We're so close..."

options.text: Leave the forest and take a different route.

2237.text:
"I don't think there's anything else for us to do in this forest," Marian says.
"At least now we know," the Commander responds, looking at Marian. "Should we head back toward the walking trail?"
"... Yeah, let's go."
The two of them make their way out of the forest and head south toward the walking trail.

2238.text:
Thump, thump, thump.
"!!!"
Marian and the Commander feel a familiar rumble beneath their feet. Convinced that it must be the Black Smith, the two of them...

options.text: Carefully search for a hiding spot, even one that might not be close.

2239.text:
"I can't believe it's already here...!" Marian shouts.
"It's gaining on us..." the Commander says.
Marian grabs him as she starts to panic.
"This way, Commander!"
Dragging him behind her, she runs into a collapsed building that's half-submerged in the lake.

2240.text: Knowing that haste demands even greater caution, Marian runs forward, pulling the Commander along with her. Soon, they come across a large building that has collapsed into the lake.

2241.text:
Inside the building, Marian stares at a pool of water. Since the building toppled into the lake, the water likely gets deeper inside.
"We have to go further in to be safe..."
The Commander glances at her worriedly. "But it's too dark to see what's in there... It seems a bit dangerous to go any further in."
Marian hesitates.

options.text: Leave and find somewhere else to hide.

2242.text:
Marian would rather submerge herself in water than let the Black Smith find them. She chooses to head deeper into the building.
Just then, a faint crackle catches the Commander's attention.
"Wait! Marian!"
"What...?"

2243.text: The two of them decide that it's too dangerous to venture into the darkness, and they run back outside.

2244.text: But it's too late. The pair come face-to-face with the Black Smith as it lands in front of them with a crash. Its tentacles rise up, ready to strike.

2245.text:
Marian predicts that it will only target her with its tentacles, since she's a Nikke.
Suddenly...
"Marian!"
She looks over at the Commander to see him running toward her. He's going to sacrifice himself to save her again, just like last time.

2246.text:
Marian pushes the Commander away. His body slams against the ground.
"Marian...?!"
She hears a tentacle coming and feels it wrap around her.

2247.text:
"Commander, duck!"
As the Commander ducks down, Marian lets loose a barrage of bullets at a tentacle coming her way. As she's firing, another tentacle grazes her side.
"Marian!"
"I'm... fine...!"
She quickly scans the surroundings. There's a utility pole leaning toward the Black Smith. She shoots it. The utility pole creaks as it falls over and crashes down onto the Black Smith.
"Now's our chance! Run, Commander!"
The two of them sprint forward in a frenzy.

2248.text:
Marian and the Commander barely make it into a dilapidated building.
She looks at the [[REDACT]]Commander[[/REDACT]]man... no, the Commander as he catches his breath. She knows what's coming. Her vision is starting to turn red.
"Com...mander."
Marian's eyes meet the man's... no, the Commander's.
His eyes widen.
"Marian, your eyes...!"
"If I... stop being me..."

2249.text:
Marian hands her gun over to the Commander.
"Please... use this to... shoot me in the head."
"What...?"
"There's... no... time..."
"But... I can't just...!"
"You'll... do it.... right?"
Marian gazes pleadingly at the [[REDACT]]Commander[[/REDACT]]man.
"Please..."
The [[REDACT]]man[[/REDACT]]Commander stares at the gun before slowly taking it. His hands are shaking. The barrel trembles as it's pointed at Marian.
The [[REDACT]]manCommander[[/REDACT]] fires.

2250.text:
"I think we can climb up this building. What do you think?" the Commander suggests.
It's steep, but it does look like they could run up the outer wall of the collapsed building. Marian hesitates, debating whether they should make their way up or search for another place to hide.
Thump, thump, thump.
As she deliberates, the Black Smith's heavy thuds grow closer.

condition.hint: Find another place to hide. If you find yourself in danger, fight to the end.

options.text: Enter the building through a broken window.

2251.text: It's far too risky to scale the wall of a building when they don't know if it's safe or not. Marian decides they should search for another building.

2252.text:
"Let's go up." The Commander hurriedly pulls Marian along and starts heading up the building.
"...Commander?"
He desperately pulls her along, as though he's trying to protect her from a terrible death. Last time, they were looking for a hiding place when she got grazed by the Black Smith's tentacle. She can't remember what happened after that, though.
"..."
The Commander's unusually frantic behavior leaves an impression on Marian as she follows after him.

2253.text:
Marian decides that running away and scaling the wall are both too dangerous. Instead, she starts examining the building's shattered windows.
After a moment she exclaims, "That one! Over this way!"
She and the Commander crawl through one of the windows and land on the other side where there's no water.

2254.text:
Marian and the Commander scramble up the building. The Commander's breathing starts to become heavy.
Noticing this, Marian shouts, "Let's take a short break...!"
He stops in his tracks and exhales deeply. "Okay...!"
He places his hand on an electrical control panel next to him. A faint vibration tickles his palm.
"Wait... This thing is still on."
He stares intently at the control panel and notices one of the indicator lights flickering irregularly.
"There must still be power..."
The Commander creaks open the cover of the control panel.
"Let me see..."
Marian starts to move over to him when she steps on a cracked window. It gives way beneath her feet.
"!!!"

2255.text:
"I think... we should be safe now."
Marian and the Commander slump onto the floor.
"..."
"..."
All of the numerous deaths they experienced just to get here weigh heavily on them. Neither one speaks for a long time. Marian starts thinking to herself.
What should they do now? How much longer do they have to be chased? How much longer do they have to live in fear? Is there nothing she can do other than run away or get eaten by that thing?
"Marian..."
She wonders how she can save the Commander. Is there any way to escape their pursuer?
"Marian..."
Should they keep hiding in here? Or should they go out and find a new hiding spot?
Or maybe...
It's better to die and restart...!
Marian feels a tap on her shoulder.
"Marian?"
"Yes?"

2256.text:
Marian looks up and sees the Commander gazing at her.
"Oh... Sorry. I got lost in thought and must not have heard..."
"You're really scared, aren't you?"
"What?" She hesitates. "Not... really."
He smiles warmly. "I see. I'm kinda scared."
"Commander..."
"I'm frustrated because I couldn't protect you before, and I'm scared that I might not be able to protect you again." He turns to face Marian. "And yet I'm still glad that you're here beside me. Isn't that weird?"
"!!!"
A realization hits her: he's the same as her. He's feeling the same things she is. Again. He wanted to protect her, just as she wanted to protect him. He wanted to save her.

2257.text:
"I... feel the same way. To be honest, I'm scared too. And yet..."
Marian returns the Commander's gaze. "I'm glad that I get to be here with you."
"Heheh, hahaha...!" The Commander gives out a joyful laugh. "I see. It wasn't just me. You wanted to protect me too. I almost forgot... Neither of us is alone. Hahaha!"
He looks warmly at Marian.
"Commander..."
"I want to get out of here." His eyes sparkle. "I want to leave this dark, cramped place, and I want to travel more with you. I want a happy future with you."
His words give Marian courage.
"So let's stop running. Let's stop letting that thing dictate our every move, and let's do whatever we can to defeat it... Let's get away from this lake."
As Marian looks at the Commander, her heart is filled with...
"Yeah, you're right. Let's defeat that thing, and then..." She pauses for a moment.
"Let's be happy together."

2258.text:
"At our current strength," the Commander says, "I don't think we'll be able to win in a head-on confrontation. Can you think of any other strategies?"
Marian tries to think of some other means of attack.

options.text: Suggest thinking about it some more.

condition.hint: Try heading deep inside somewhere close to hide.

2259.text:
They agree to think about it some more, and continue pondering for some time. However, no matter how much they think it over, they can't come up with a solution.
"Marian, maybe we should just go outside first and..." The man looks at Marian. "Oh."
Marian stares back at him, her eyes red.
"I guess... it's already time."

2260.text:
Marian thinks back on one of her memories.
"Remember when I got electrocuted by that high-voltage current? What if we electrocuted it?"
"You want to electrocute it?"
"The most dangerous thing about the Black Smith is its tentacles," she says. "If we can shock it with a surge of high-voltage electricity to prevent it from using them, even if only for a moment... we could use that opening to destroy its core!"
She looks at the Commander with conviction. "I think that's how we defeat it."
"That's a great idea. As for how we electrocute it..." The Commander recalls something, too. "The control panel for this building is still operational, right?"
"Oh, that time we fell through the window...!"
"Exactly. If we can send that current through the flooded area we fell into..."
"Then we might just be able to electrocute it!"
The Commander rises to his feet.
"Let's go, Marian. It may not work the first time, but we'll keep trying over and over..." He reaches out a hand to her. "Until we win."
She takes his hand. "Yeah!"
The two of them head outside together.

2261.text:
The two of them step outside and climb the building once again, taking care not to fall through any windows. Once they reach the electrical panel, Marian opens it and checks inside. It appears to be a control mechanism used to supply power to the building's facilities, as well as the exterior lighting. Most of the indicator lights are off, but a single circuit to the side glows red.
"Commander."
Marian looks down past the window they fell through before. A power cable connected to a damaged exterior unit hangs limp beyond the shattered window, dipping straight into the lakewater.
"I think we can use this. The only problem is, I'm not sure it'll carry enough current all the way down..."
Marian gazes at the breaker lever.
"I think we'll have to throw the switch to know for sure."
"Let's give it a shot."
"Okay...! We'll need to pull the lever at the right moment in order to conserve as much power as possible, though."
"Which means..."
Marian looks at the Commander with firm resolve.

2262.text:
"No, absolutely n—"
"You said you wanted us to have a happy future, right? And we will." Marian's eyes sparkle. "I'll act as the bait and lure the Black Smith here. As for you, you need to pull the lever at just the right moment."
"Marian..."
"Can you do that?"
The Commander stares at Marian for a moment.
"Okay," he says. "I'll time it just right and make sure we succeed."
"Great!"
"Let me at least go with you until you reach the ground, though. I think I'll be too scared if I wait here alone."
She looks at him. His eyes are filled with concern for her being alone out there. It reminds her of the days when she was desperately lonely.
"Sure..."
That is why, when she looks into his warm eyes...
"Commander."
"Yeah?"
... She smiles.
"Thank you."

2263.text:
Marian and the Commander stand together in front of the collapsed building.
Thump, thump, thump.
They feel familiar tremors coming from a distance.
"Black Smith detected."
"Good. I'll head back up to the electrical panel."
"I'll lure it into position and join you right after."
"Watch out for the tentacles, and for the windows."
"Hehe. You be careful of the windows too."
The Commander smiles and dashes up the outer wall first. Marian watches him go, then fixes her gaze straight ahead. The Black Smith comes into view.
"Just a little closer...!"
It lashes a tentacle out toward Marian.
"Now!"

2264.text:
Marian frantically sprints up the building as quickly as she can.
Thump, thump, thump!
The Black Smith rapidly closes in behind her.
"Just a bit more... Just a bit more...!"
Thump, thump thump...!
It runs before leaping up and slamming down onto the building.
"Just a bit more...!!"
Its foot plunges through a window with a loud crash, sending a giant current of water throughout the inside of the building.
This is the moment!
"Commander!"
The Commander pulls the lever.

2265.text: Thinking back on the time she fell through the window, Marian looks down at her feet and cautiously runs up.

2266.text:
A surge of electricity crackles through the water. For a moment, the Black Smith grinds to a halt.
"Now's our chance!"
Marian and the Commander unleash a concentrated flurry of fire straight at the Black Smith's core.
"Please...!"
"Break!"
The core begins to crack.

2267.text:
The core shatters, and the Black Smith finally crashes to the ground with a loud thud.
"The Black Smith is unresponsive... Target down...!"
Marian turns to the Commander and looks at him with trembling eyes.
"Commander...!"
The Commander stares back at her with the same emotion in his eyes.
"Marian...!"
They pull each other into a tight embrace. They finally defeated the Black Smith that had driven Marian to her death so many times before.

2268.text:
Marian and the Commander make their way down the building and continue along the walking trail. Though they cross paths with several groups of Raptures along the way, they are easily able to dispatch them.
They walk on and on, until...
"The trail ends here... finally," Marian says.
"Yeah..."
The Commander looks ahead.
The ruins of what had once been dubbed "the new city" welcome them.

2269.text:
"We made it... We really made it. Honestly... I never thought I'd make it even halfway here."
"We made it because we're together," the Commander says, looking at her. "Because we have each other."
Behind him, the sky is painted gold.
"Marian."
Golden light washes over him as he smiles at her.
"Thank you for putting your trust in me that day. Let's continue to survive, and make it to the end. Together."
Their life before them shines a gold hue, as brightly as the lake they once gazed upon— brighter, even.
"And then... let's keep going, and face the future. Together."
There he stands, right in the middle of that golden light. And there she is, right next to him.
"Yes, Commander."

2270.text:
Twilight envelops the sky as the pair walk toward the entrance of the new city.
"What should we do first once we get there?" the Commander asks. "Maybe find somewhere to set up base? I hope we don't have to face another Black Smith, or anything like that."
The gold of dusk changes into a deep scarlet.
"It might be smart to find a place we can use as a trap first. Or maybe secure some food..."
The sun sinks a little lower.
"Hopefully there's somewhere we can rest easy, even just a little bit. We went through so much this time."
The world is dyed red.
"What do you think, Marian?"

2271.text:
"Oh."
Marian turns to look at him. Her eyes are glowing red.
"It's already time..."
The man grabs Marian's arm.
"You're going to go, even if I ask you not to, aren't you?"
"I'm going."
Her gun clicks...

options.text: [[REDACT]]Don't do it! Don't kill him! Please![[/REDACT]]Kill the man.

2301.text:
